what: Split PDF takes one PDF and pulls out only the pages you choose. You can save those pages together as one new PDF, or save every chosen page as its own small PDF inside a ZIP file.

It is useful when you only need one chapter of a long report, one page of a contract to sign, or when a website asks you to upload each page as a separate file. You type the page numbers, pick the output, and download.
The file is opened and split inside your browser. Nothing is uploaded, so it is safe for private documents.
uses: Send only the pages that matter
Extract pages 4 to 6 of a 40-page report and send just those to a colleague.
If several documents were scanned into one PDF, extract each document into its own file.
Some upload forms want each page separately. Choose the ZIP output to get one PDF per page.
Pages come out in the order you type them, so you can build a new PDF with a different page order.
Extract the first few pages of an e-book or report to share as a preview.
tutorial: Click "Click or drop a PDF here" or drag one PDF onto the box. The tool shows the file name and how many pages it has, for example "report.pdf · 24 pages".
Look at the "Pages to extract" box
It is filled in for you with every page, such as 1-24. Change it to the pages you want. Use commas between items and a hyphen for a range, for example 1-3, 7, 10-12.
Pick "One PDF with these pages" to get one file that holds all the chosen pages. Pick "A separate PDF for every page (ZIP)" to get one small PDF for each chosen page, packed in a ZIP file.
The tool shows "Working…" and then a green message such as "Extracted 5 pages" or "Created 5 PDFs" with the size of the result.
Click "Download". One PDF is named like report-pages.pdf. A ZIP is named like report-pages.zip and holds files such as report-page-3.pdf, where the number is the page number in the original.
You do not need to load the file again. Change the page list or the output and click "Split PDF" again to make another file.
features: Mix single pages and ranges in one line, such as 2, 5-8, 11.
Save the chosen pages as one PDF, or as one PDF per page in a ZIP.
Pages are placed in the order you type, so 5, 1-3 starts with page 5.
If you list the same page twice, it is included only once.
If you type a page that does not exist, the tool tells you which part is wrong and how many pages the PDF has.
Pages are copied, not redrawn, so text stays selectable and images keep their quality.

example.title: Worked example: extract a chapter and the index
example.text: Ravi has handbook.pdf with 60 pages. He needs chapter 3 (pages 15 to 22) and the index (page 60). He loads the file, replaces 1-60 with 15-22, 60, and keeps "One PDF with these pages". After clicking "Split PDF" he sees "Extracted 9 pages". He downloads handbook-pages.pdf, which has 9 pages: the eight chapter pages followed by the index.

tips: To split the whole PDF into single pages, keep the default range (for example 1-24) and choose the ZIP output.
Spaces do not matter: "1-3,5" and "1 - 3, 5" give the same result.
To remove a few pages instead of keeping a few, Delete PDF Pages may be quicker.
Most computers open a ZIP file with a double-click. On a phone, use the Files app to unzip it.
Your original PDF is never changed. You always get a new file.
problems: The message says a page "is outside this PDF"
You typed a page number larger than the page count, or a range that goes backwards like 8-3. Check the page count shown under the box and fix the range.
The message says something "is not a page number or range"
Only numbers, commas and hyphens are allowed. Remove words like "page" or "to", and write 3-5 instead of 3 to 5.
The page box is grey and I cannot type
The box only becomes active after a PDF has loaded. Choose a file first. If a red message appears, the file may be damaged or password protected.
I expected separate files but got one PDF
Change "Output" to "A separate PDF for every page (ZIP)" and click "Split PDF" again.
